description_full: DigitalOcean Holdings, Inc., through its subsidiaries, operates an agentic inference cloud platform in North America, Europe, Asia, and internationally. The company provides AI and Digital Native Enterprises build, run, and scale intelligent applications for growing technology companies. It also offers infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS) solutions comprising compute, storage, and networking products, including cloud firewalls, managed load balancers, NAT gateways, and virtual private cloud software, as well as IP address management and domain name system management. In addition, the company provides platform-as-a-service (PaaS) and software-as-a-service (SaaS) solutions, such as managed databases; managed Kubernetes and container registry; application platform to build, deploy, and scale applications; Functions, a serverless compute solution; and Uptime for real-time uptime and latency alerts, as well as managed hosting and DigitalOcean Marketplace, a platform where developers can find pre-configured applications and solutions. Further, it offers artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) applications comprising GPU droplets; bare metal GPUS, which provides access to a GPU server without any virtualization layer and gives developers with customizable server for their use case; and Jupyter Notebooks that provides cloud workspace and managed interactive development environment for exploring data and training, and building machine learning models. Its customers use its platform in various industry verticals, such as online gaming, fintech, and cybersecurity, as well as for a range of use cases, including building and hosting websites, web and mobile applications development, AI integration, and building AI products and applications. DigitalOcean Holdings, Inc. was incorporated in 2012 and is headquartered in Broomfield, Colorado.

financial_summary: DigitalOcean Holdings, Inc. is a mid-cap technology business with a $8.6B market cap on $901M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +16% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +5.0pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 1% against a 11% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 60% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $181M in free cash flow — roughly 20 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.19× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.5× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 8.8×.
Shareholder yield is only 1.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 17% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

sect: Its 17% operating margin runs 10pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It earns less of the sector's profit than its revenue share would suggest (0.74x).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 530 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 178% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 42% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 61% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 90% and a beta of 1.46, it amplifies market moves.
Liquidity is deep, with about $274.7M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 69% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $22.30 (margin of safety -225%), so there is no valuation cushion.
On multiples it looks expensive against Technology peers: P/E 249.9 vs 26.7, EV/EBITDA 28.5 vs 16.4 and P/FCF 47.4 vs 25.4 (sector median).
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 2.1% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 1.6% (vs the 8% bar).
The 15 covering analysts target $165 on average, 127% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 1% falls short of the cost of capital of 11.0%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 2.43).
It runs a 60% gross margin and converts 20% of revenue into free cash flow, or 11% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 8/9 and cash conversion of 1.19x.
Operating margin is running 13pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 17.9% of revenue on R&D and 8.9% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: Leverage is heavy at 3.5x net debt to EBITDA ($254.5M of cash against $1.3B of debt), with interest covered 8.8x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 3.4, in the safe zone).
The current ratio of 0.69 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 16.1% over 3 years.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (0.9x, 14.3% of sales), a maintenance pace.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 49.5% on average.
own: Insiders own 16.6%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 82%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (6 sales, net $4.9M sold).
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.0% (1.0% in buybacks).
The share count has grown 1.9% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
Short interest is elevated at 11.4% of the float, 4.0 days to cover.
people: With about 1,462 employees, each generates about $617K of revenue, 1.7x the Technology median, and productivity has risen 20.4% a year.
That works out to $123K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $1.2M (2x revenue per employee).
